source: Bush, R. 2010. 'Large Ruminant Nutrition Theory, Part 2: Silages and Better Feeding Practices', University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com), including a Village Livestock Agent (VLA) fattening-cattle feeding trial conducted in Tbong Khmum, Aug-Dec 2009. Same font/ligature encoding quirk as Source O, decoded the same way.
text: A Village Livestock Agent (VLA) fattening trial run in Tbong Khmum province from August to December 2009 (4 months) compared three feeding groups on paired cattle: Group 1 (grass plus legume supplement, no rice straw) produced weight gains from roughly 134-136kg to 159-172kg per animal, with sale value roughly doubling (from 600,000 to 900,000-950,000 riel); Group 2 (grass plus rice straw, no legume) produced larger gains, from 134-169kg to 191-229kg, with value increasing from 600,000-700,000 riel to 1,000,000-1,200,000 riel; Group 3 (free grazing 5 hours/day, no supplementation) produced the smallest gains, from 151-225kg to 169-256kg, with value increasing from 600,000-1,100,000 to 680,000-1,300,000 riel. Across all groups, condition score improved by roughly 0.5-1.5 points over the 4 months. The trial's broader point for extension purposes is to demonstrate to farmers, using their own animals, that supplementing young leafy grass and a protein source (legume or rice bran/maize meal) produces materially better growth and sale value than grass-only or free-grazing alone -- with a suggested example ration of 80% young fertilised grass mixed with 20% legume leaf (e.g. Stylo or Leucaena) plus 1kg of rice bran or maize meal per day.
caveat: This is a single 4-month field trial with a small number of paired animals per group (illustrative extension demonstration data, not a large-scale controlled study) -- useful as a real Cambodia-specific example but not a guaranteed outcome for every herd.
